questions.q: How does translation differ fundamentally from revaluation?
options: They are the same process with different names
Translation restates an entire ledger's balances into a different reporting currency; revaluation corrects specific foreign-currency-exposed balances within a ledger
Translation only applies to expense accounts
Revaluation applies to an entire ledger, while translation only applies to one account
questions.explain: Revaluation targets specific exposed balances within a ledger; translation restates the whole ledger into another currency for reporting purposes.

questions.q: Which rate is used to translate balance sheet accounts, and why?
options: The period average rate, because balance sheet accounts accumulate over the whole period
The period-end spot rate, because a balance sheet is a snapshot as of that date
The original transaction-date rate, never updated
There is no rate used for balance sheet accounts
questions.explain: Because a balance sheet reflects a single point in time, it is translated using the period-end spot rate.

questions.q: Why are income statement accounts translated using a period average rate instead of the period-end rate?
options: Because income statement activity accumulated throughout the period, not just on the last day
Because income statement accounts never involve foreign currency
Because average rates are always higher than spot rates
Because Oracle Fusion does not support translating income statement accounts
questions.explain: Since income statement activity builds up over the whole period, an average rate better represents that accumulated activity than a single point-in-time rate.

questions.q: What is the Cumulative Translation Adjustment (CTA)?
options: An error that must be corrected before period close
A dedicated equity account that absorbs the imbalance created by translating balance sheet and income statement accounts at two different rates
A type of intercompany balancing rule
A report confirming journal approvals
questions.explain: The CTA is the expected plug in equity that reconciles the imbalance from using the period-end rate on the balance sheet and the average rate on the income statement.

questions.q: Does translation change the original ledger's books, for example LTV Manufacturing UK Ltd's GBP ledger?
options: Yes, translation permanently overwrites the original currency's balances
No, translation produces a separate reporting-currency view for consolidation while leaving the original ledger's books unchanged
Only the income statement accounts are changed, not the balance sheet
Translation deletes the original ledger after running
questions.explain: Translation is a reporting output, not a restatement of the subsidiary's own books, which remain in their original currency.
